idiom_name: unused-result warning by default, @discardableResult as the opt-out, Result
implementation_notes: Swift flipped the default with SE-0047: calling a function or method that returns a non-Void value without using the result produces a warning, and @discardableResult is the explicit opt-out for the ones that are genuinely procedures - the Swift book defines the attribute exactly that way. That makes the returned value part of the contract by default, since the caller must either use it or write _ = to discard it, while Result<Success, Failure> carries failure as a returned value for callers that want to inspect it instead of propagating it. Keep @discardableResult rare: it erases the guarantee for that API, and imported Objective-C declarations receive it automatically.
pitfalls: Imported Objective-C APIs that are not marked warn_unused_result are automatically annotated @discardableResult, so the warning is silently absent exactly where misuse is common.
Writing _ = f() silences the warning with no trace, so a reviewer cannot see that a result was meant to be checked unless the discard is commented.
@discardableResult belongs to the declaration, not the value: assigning the function to a variable loses it, and calling through that variable warns again.
